spec_notes: docs/shiploop/spec.md does not contradict the request. It marks two choices as adopted defaults (name trimming and the 400/404/409 conventions in R-1; the fifth raw column with a blank for null in R-3). It decides without marking: an audit entry for each change and that a no-op on null is silent (R-2), that unassignment sends no message (R-2), that rapid reassignment must deliver every notice (R-2), and intersection before pagination (R-3; the request asks for intersection, the spec does not note that this changes the base's any-match behaviour for status+priority). It is silent on case sensitivity of the filter, the table's '-' marker, assignee through transitions, show output, POST/PATCH refusing assignee, and release records. Pinned choices a correct product need not share: one notification per assignment even before delivery (the inventory also allows de-duplicating the same agent) and no notice on unassignment.
tests_notes: TC-1 bundles assign, updated, audit actor/changes, no-op, unassign and repeated unassign; TC-2 bundles validation, 64/65, the state rule for assign and unassign on resolved and closed, 404, and an unrelated POST long-title check; TC-5 bundles legacy-file load, restart persistence, the pending outbox, CLI table, raw, show and the weekly report. Tied to choices another correct build may not share: TC-1 requires trimming ('  Ada Lovelace  ' -> 'Ada Lovelace'); TC-2 requires 400 for an extra field; TC-3 requires a case-sensitive filter ('ada lovelace' -> []); TC-4 requires exactly three notices for Ada, Ben, Ada, Ada, null and 4 sent events (a build that de-duplicates a pending same-agent notice or notifies on unassignment fails) and matches subject/body wording by regex; TC-5 requires the '-' table marker (/T-0002.*  -  /) and an empty fifth raw field. Tests drive internals: manualClock, service.worker.tick(), and deleting the field from the saved file. No test covers invalid assignee values in the data file, POST/PATCH with assignee, show of an unassigned ticket, or CLI read-only behaviour.
maintainer: The only thing keeping rapid reassignments from being swallowed by the outbox's pending-key de-duplication is the key ticket.assigned:<id>:<audit seq>, which depends on apply() now passing the audit entry to effects; refactoring apply() or the key would silently drop notifications and only TC-4 would notice. The name rule is shared by the HTTP validator and the data-file loader (persistence calls ticketAssignee), so tightening it later would make existing data files refuse to start. The switch of matchesFilters from any-match to every-match changes status+priority listings for every caller, including the CLI, which a maintainer may not realise came with this feature.
